claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm inquiring about my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that context! So you're inquiring about your son **Alex**. 

To determine eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather some information about your circumstances.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 18.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex is 18 years old.

**Is Alex still in full-time education or approved training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education or training anymore.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Alex is 18 and not in full-time education or approved training.

**Is Alex in paid work or self-employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he works full-time at a local shop.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**What is Alex's gross weekly income from his employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of the exact amount, but he works full-time hours - around 35-40 hours a week at the shop.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate that information. To be thorough, let me ask:

**Do you know approximately how much Alex earns per week, or what his hourly rate is?** This will help me determine if he meets the income thresholds for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I think he earns around £10 an hour, so probably around £350-400 a week working full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that estimate. That's helpful context.

Now, I have a few more questions to complete the eligibility assessment:

**Are you Alex's parent and his primary carer, or do you have parental responsibility for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his parent and he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?** (This relates to your immigration status, which is relevant for Child Benefit eligibility.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming you're in the UK. Just to clarify for the eligibility assessment:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status under the UK's immigration rules?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

I now have sufficient information to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit. Let me review the key details:

- **Child:** Alex, age 18
- **Education/Training:** Not in full-time education or approved training
- **Employment:** Working full-time (35-40 hours per week) at approximately £10/hour (estimated £350-400 per week)
- **Parent:** You are Alex's parent with parental responsibility, living in the UK
- **Immigration Status:** You are a British citizen

Based on UK Child Benefit rules, children aged 16-19 can qualify for Child Benefit if they are in full-time education or approved training. However, Alex is no longer in education or training and is in full-time paid employment instead.

Unfortunately, this means Alex does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit, as he is over 16 and not in qualifying education or training.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:**

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex. 

**Why:** Alex is 18 years old and working in full-time paid employment. To qualify for Child Benefit at this age, he would need to be in full-time education or an approved training course. Since he's no longer studying and is instead in paid work, he doesn't meet the eligibility requirements.

If you have any other questions or if there are other children you'd like me to assess, please let me know.
